blogs.title: Why Tokenization May Be Obsolete: Introducing Byte‑Level Patches
blogs.description: An accessible overview of the motivation behind moving away from fixed vocabularies. The post explains how traditional tokenizers bias models, what “patches” are, and why grouping raw bytes dynamically can give models a more faithful view of language. Readers will walk away with a clear intuition for why the Byte Latent Transformer (BLT) treats bytes as first‑class citizens.

blogs.title: Dynamic Patching Explained: Letting Entropy Decide the Chunk Size
blogs.description: A deep‑dive into BLT’s core innovation—entropy‑based patching. The article breaks down how a tiny byte‑level LM estimates next‑byte uncertainty, how thresholds turn high‑entropy spots into patch boundaries, and why this lets the model allocate more compute where it matters most. Visual examples show patches growing on easy text and shrinking on tricky passages.

blogs.title: Inside the BLT Architecture: Byte Encoders, a Global Latent Transformer, and Decoders
blogs.description: A step‑by‑step tour of BLT’s three‑block design. We unpack the lightweight local encoder that turns bytes into latent patches, the large global transformer that operates on those patches, and the decoder that reconstructs bytes. The post also highlights cross‑attention tricks and n‑gram hash embeddings that make the system both powerful and efficient.

blogs.title: Scaling Laws at Byte Level: How Patches Beat Tokens on Compute‑Optimal Training
blogs.description: Translates the paper’s scaling experiments into plain language. We compare flop‑controlled training curves for BLT versus Llama 3, illustrate how larger patches reduce inference FLOPs, and show why BLT can grow both model size and patch size while staying within a fixed inference budget. Graphs are reinterpreted for non‑technical readers.

blogs.title: Robustness Benefits of Modeling Raw Bytes: From Noisy Text to Low‑Resource Languages
blogs.description: Shows concrete examples of BLT’s superior handling of corrupted input, character‑level tasks, phoneme transcription, and translation of under‑represented scripts. The post explains why direct byte access gives the model built‑in orthographic knowledge that tokenizers lose, backed by benchmark results from CUTE, G2P, and FLORES‑101.

blogs.title: From Llama 3 to BLT: “Byte‑ifying” Existing Tokenizer Models
blogs.description: Explains the distillation technique where a pretrained tokenizer‑based model seeds the global transformer of BLT. Readers learn how this shortcut can dramatically cut training FLOPs while retaining most of the original model’s knowledge—and why this could be a practical path to adopting byte‑level LLMs in industry.
